title: How should the Windows installer be signed?
lead: Pick how the installer gets signed so Windows stops saying 'Unknown publisher'. I recommend A: Microsoft's Artifact Signing at $9.99 a month, if you sign up as an individual in the US or Canada. Confidence: medium.
for_you: The warning shows your name instead of 'Unknown publisher'; it still appears for a few weeks until Windows trusts the app

for_you.text: You sign up for an Azure subscription and an ID check (one evening); an agent wires it into the release build
A monthly charge you can cancel any time; unsigned releases keep working

context: Release v0.1.0 is unsigned, so Windows shows 'Windows protected your PC' with More info, Run anyway. install-research (memo M030): no certificate removes that warning on day one; every signed app still warns until it builds reputation ('several weeks and hundreds of clean installs', Microsoft). Only a Microsoft Store MSIX avoids it at once. EV certificates stopped skipping the warning in August 2024. A Microsoft Store individual developer account is free since 2025, but Tauri makes EXE/MSI, the Store's EXE route still needs a paid certificate, and the free MSIX route for Tauri is experimental. Prices as found on 2026-11-13.

options.name: Microsoft Artifact Signing
options.summary: Microsoft's cloud signing service, $9.99 a month, no hardware token, plugs into Tauri's sign command. Open to individuals in the USA and Canada only (organizations also EU and UK).
pros: Cheapest real signing, about $120 a year
No USB token; signs from the build on your PC
cons: Individuals only in the US or Canada; needs a paid Azure subscription and ID check
options.effort: Small: sign-up, then a sign command in the release build

options.name: OV certificate
options.summary: A standard code-signing certificate from a seller such as Sectigo, about $150-300 a year, key on a USB token or cloud HSM, renewed at most every 460 days.
cons: About twice the price, plus a token to manage

options.name: Stay unsigned for now
options.summary: Keep releasing unsigned; the docs tell users to choose More info, Run anyway. Try a free Microsoft Store listing later.

recommendation: A is the cheapest signing that shows your name, and with no token it fits the build on your PC. Skip EV: it no longer buys anything.
change_mind: If you can't register as a US or Canadian individual, B; if the app stays mostly for you for now, C.

settles.value: unsigned for now; docs tell users More info, Run anyway; Microsoft Artifact Signing is the first choice if signing is taken up later
